description: "Read forecast and historical workbooks, select tables and inspect the observation contract."

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reading REQ workbooks}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

REQ editions normally publish separate forecast and historical workbooks.
Use `read_req_forecasts()` and `read_req_history()` when the source surface
matters, or use `read_req()` with an exact release ID when a coherent combined
view is needed. The examples below use the package's small synthetic
workbooks, so they parse without discovery, download or credentials.

## Read both workbook surfaces

```{r read-workbooks}
library(readreq)

forecast_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx", package = "readreq"
)
history_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "readreq-example-history.xlsx", package = "readreq"
)
if (!nzchar(forecast_path)) {
  forecast_path <- file.path(
    "..", "inst", "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx"
  )
}
if (!nzchar(history_path)) {
  history_path <- file.path(
    "..", "inst", "extdata", "readreq-example-history.xlsx"
  )
}
stopifnot(
  nzchar(forecast_path), file.exists(forecast_path),
  nzchar(history_path), file.exists(history_path)
)

cache_dir <- tempfile("readreq-workbook-cache-")
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
forecast <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path, view = "reported", cache_dir = cache_dir
)
history <- read_req_history(
  history_path, view = "reported", cache_dir = cache_dir
)

c(forecast_rows = nrow(forecast), history_rows = nrow(history))
table(forecast$period_status, useNA = "ifany")
table(history$frequency, useNA = "ifany")
```

`view = "reported"` preserves admitted source presentations. The
asset-specific readers also support `view = "canonical"`, which resolves
documented within-workbook duplication. `read_req(..., view = "current")`
applies the checked-in precedence policy across forecast and historical
assets when an exact release bundle is available.

## Select stable tables and filters

Table IDs are preferable to relying on workbook order. Source aliases are
also accepted where they are documented by the installed source catalogue.

```{r select-tables}
iron_ore <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path,
  sheets = "forecast_iron_ore",
  commodities = "Iron ore",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

monthly <- read_req_history(
  history_path,
  tables = "history_monthly_benchmark_prices",
  frequency = "monthly",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

list(
  forecast_tables = unique(iron_ore$table_id),
  history_tables = unique(monthly$table_id),
  forecast_columns = names(iron_ore),
  history_columns = names(monthly)
)
```

Filters reduce the selected output; they do not change the semantic identity
of a series. `series_id` identifies the semantic dimensions, while
`observation_key` combines that identity with the target period. Use
`req_observation_schema()` when a downstream table or validation step needs
the complete field contract.

```{r inspect-contract}
schema <- req_observation_schema()
schema[, c("field", "type", "required")]

head(
  iron_ore[, c(
    "series_id", "observation_key", "period", "period_start", "period_end",
    "period_status", "unit", "value", "source_dataset", "source_sheet",
    "sha256", "parser_version"
  )]
)
```

## Reports and unsupported structures

The normal path reads workbook assets; it does not OCR report PDFs. The two
report-only editions (`req-2011-12` and `req-2013-03`) use an audited report
table fallback. That fallback requires the `pdftotext` executable from
Poppler and exact audited PDF bytes. Poppler is not needed for ordinary
workbook reads. Unknown workbook layouts, unexplained values in numeric
regions and ambiguous units fail with typed conditions rather than silently
guessing a parser result.
